newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: No deal with Peru rebels, says Malaysia minister.
newsitem.headline: No deal with Peru rebels, says Malaysia minister.

text.p: Malaysia's Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi has said he was not trying to cut a deal with Marxist rebels in Lima to secure the release of Malaysia's ambassador to Peru, the Bernama news agency reported on Friday.
Malaysian ambassador Ahmad Mokhtar Selat is being held with 102 other VIPs at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima by rebels belonging to the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA).
"That's not how we work. My arrival was known to the media. We can't be doing that (negotiating on our own)," Abdullah was quoted as saying in a telephone interview.
Abdullah met with Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori in Lima on Thursday and was briefed on the hostage crisis.

Abdullah's arrival in Lima, to carry out a "special mission" on the instruction of Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, had sparked speculation that the minister was trying to cut a private deal with the rebels.
Abdullah refuted such speculation, saying Malaysia had faith in Fujimori and supported all appropriate measures and actions taken by his government to resolve the 10-day old crisis.
"He (Fujimori) can control the situation. He is calm, although serious. He knows exactly what is happening. Just have to keep working on it," Bernama quoted Abdullah as saying.
